🇲🇽📰 <u>PROTECT THE PRESS — AND FINALLY CLOSE THE CASES</u>

On International Journalists' Day, Mexico's National Human Rights Commission (CNDH) called to "strengthen actions to protect journalists and guarantee the right to inform," while admitting there is still "a debt in the investigation and resolution of cases of violence" — above all at the local level, where organized crime reaches. It credited eight years of advances in press protection and its round-the-clock protection program, but was clear the risk hasn't gone. Impunity, not shortage of words, is the unfinished part.

🇲🇽🗳️ <u>THE RIGHT WANTS ONE VOTE PER HOUSEHOLD — NOT PER WOMAN</u>

PAN activist Javier Albarrán has floated "household voting" in Mexico — concentrating a family's ballots in one person to strengthen "the family as society's basic cell." UNAM political scientist Ana Karen Cortés warns of "very important networks and power groups seeking to eliminate the participation of women and historically marginalized groups." Mexican women have only held citizenship for three or four generations; the tradwife-to-household-vote pipeline, imported straight from Turning Point USA, is built to claw that back.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>NO MORE UNTOUCHABLES: SAT TO AUDIT UNIONS AND GOVERNORS</u>

Sheinbaum's 2027 budget bill would put unions and state and municipal governments under the tax authority (SAT) — bodies long exempt from real fiscal scrutiny. The initiative wants the SAT to verify their income "matches its purpose and complies with the tax provisions applicable to them." Until now unions kept no accounting and issued no tax receipts, while local governments only had to withhold and remit — feeding the perception they answered to no one. That perception is what's ending.

⚖️🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO'S TOP COURT: HOME-COOKED CANNABIS IS A RIGHT</u>

Mexico's Supreme Court ruled 7-2 that an adult with a personal-use permit can cook cannabis into their own food — brownies, edibles, all of it — calling it "an ordinary culinary activity," not pharmaceutical manufacturing subject to special sanitary controls. Justice Lenia Batres's project orders Cofepris to grant the permit; sale, distribution and supply to others stay banned. While Marco Rubio lectures Mexico on drugs, its own courts keep widening personal freedom on Mexican terms.

🇲🇽🛢️ <u>Mexico slashes Pemex debt bailouts nearly 70% — and bets the oil giant posts a surplus</u>

Mexico's 2027 budget cuts federal support for Pemex's debt payments by nearly 70% — from 263.5 billion pesos this year to 81.1 billion — while Hacienda projects the state oil company will post a 95.1-billion-peso ($5.6B) financial surplus, per El Financiero's read of the Paquete Económico. A decade after neoliberal governments left it for dead, Pemex is being weaned off the direct bailouts that once defined it.

🇲🇽🔋 <u>Mexico's public utility builds a green-hydrogen 'Oasis' to power 40,000 homes</u>

State utility CFE is developing "Oasis," a solar-plus-green-hydrogen project in Mulegé, Baja California Sur: 60 MW of generation and 20 MW of battery storage powering 40,000 households, while cutting 23,000 m³ of fuel oil and diesel a year and 93,000 tons of CO₂ — the equivalent of pulling 31,463 cars off the road, in a region that until now burned shipped-in diesel. Built and owned by the public utility neoliberals spent years trying to dismantle.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Another arrest in the murder of Michoacán mayor Carlos Manzo — 32 now detained</u>

Federal forces captured Alexis "El Vikingo" Medina García in Zapopan, a CJNG regional operator in Uruapan accused in the assassination of Michoacán mayor Carlos Manzo and said to have taken over the local cell after his predecessor's arrest last November. It's the 32nd detention tied to the case — a joint operation of the security ministry, the FGR, Sedena, the Navy, the National Guard and Michoacán state prosecutors.

🩺🇲🇽 <u>CNDH exposes the hidden cost of Mexico's hospitals: exhausted, abused medical residents</u>

Mexico's human-rights commission (CNDH) documented a structural crisis for medical residents — on-call shifts past 24 hours, gender violence, and a legal limbo that treats them as students rather than workers. "The health system cannot be strengthened if those who sustain it in shifts, emergencies and operating rooms face precarious conditions," the CNDH warned. First-year residency slots doubled from 2020 to 2025; in February the IMSS began scrapping the 24-hour-plus shifts.

🇲🇽💧 <u>No special treatment: CFE cuts power to LeBarón wells over million-peso debts</u>

In drought-stricken Chihuahua, state utility CFE pulled the power on farm wells — including those of the LeBarón Mormon colony, well-known 4T critics — over debts of up to 2 million pesos, some unpaid for more than a decade. The wells lost their 95% federal energy subsidy in May because they pump water with no concession title from Conagua. The LeBarón blocked a highway and held CFE trucks for 24 hours; Adrián LeBarón accused the government of "politicizing" a bill nobody denies exists.
banner: CFE CUTS LEBARÓN WELLS OVER UNPAID DEBTS

⚖️🇲🇽 <u>Mexico's elected Supreme Court shields workers' pensions from the taxman</u>

Mexico's newly elected Supreme Court ruled 6–3 that when a worker dies, the family inheriting their Afore retirement savings pays zero income tax — the money "belonged to the worker, accumulated over a lifetime of labor," so it counts as a legacy, not taxable income. The dissent wanted it taxed "in defense of the public treasury." The court sided with the families.
